requirements.identity: Mention payload attributes retain application key separately from persistent block ID and display value. Person IDs, document IDs beginning with /, Unicode, optional icons, cover references, and private JSON fields stay exact.
requirements.projection: Existing [label](mention:identifier) syntax encodes identifiers and escapes display syntax. Empty strings, literal at-signs, Markdown/MDX-looking text, whitespace, CR/LF/tab, and entity-looking strings parse back exactly. Raw link source positions remain available.
requirements.compatibility: Link-style display labels remain atomic. The captured raw @mention transform remains unchanged, including its historical traversal behavior. Both original parser parity oracles pass without reference or assertion edits.
requirements.nativeInsertion: A locked inline content control, alias, and payload record commit as one native history unit. Word fallback normalizes line boundaries only; an empty display uses the key. Duplicate IDs, invalid positions, stale reads, suggestion mode, and unprepared rooms refuse before writes.
requirements.propertyOwnership: Label syntax and identifier syntax have separate property spans. Escaped values expose no direct substring write range. Native source-map lookups resolve the correct payload field.
requirements.tables: Mention serialization declares literal GFM-safe cell syntax. Native mention controls preserve GFM tables without promoting them to HTML. Rich opaque serializers retain their existing HTML requirement.
requirements.nativeFidelity: Exact metadata, imported inline/display OMML fingerprints, fallback text, package history, native typing on both control boundaries, and DOCX save/reopen pass.
requirements.sharedScenario: Two fixed client orders times two delivery receivers. Concurrent person/document insertion, deletion during peer editing, both independent histories, reconnect, remote geometry, exact main Word and saved convergence, DOCX/room reopening, and unchanged Yjs snapshots across projection reads pass.
